meta.title: Ember — AI Observability — Crucible
meta.description: Cross-tool AI assistant observability. Your data never leaves your infrastructure.

hero.headline: See how your AI tools are actually used.
hero.subheadline: Version-aware telemetry for AI coding environments. Which skills, which versions, which agents, which cost — from Forge compiler manifest to Grafana. Your data never leaves your infrastructure.

items.title: No idea which skills are deployed
items.description: You sync 20 skills to 50 developers. Which version is each developer running? Are all teams on the latest? No way to know.

items.title: No cost attribution
items.description: Langfuse shows total LLM cost. But which skill caused it? Did skill v2.1 cost 40% more than v2.0? Nobody can answer this.

items.title: Trust problem
items.description: Any observability tool that phones home to a third party is dead on arrival in enterprise. Data must stay in your infra.

architecture.heading: Prometheus model for AI assistants
architecture.diagramAlt: Ember Architecture — collector ingests from AI assistants and pushes to company backend
architecture.caption: Crucible provides the collector. Company provides the destination. Zero data touches Crucible servers.

loop.heading: The closed feedback loop
loop.description: Forge manages what configs/skills agents get. Ember measures how those configs/skills are actually used. Together: configure → measure → optimize.

items.title: For Engineering Managers
items.description: "How much are we spending on AI per team? Which teams are actually using the tools we paid for? What's the ROI?"

items.title: For Platform Teams
items.description: "Which skills are used? Which should we deprecate? Are developers accepting or reverting AI suggestions?"

items.title: For Compliance & Security
items.description: "Audit trail of AI usage. Proof that guardrails are applied. Data stays in our infrastructure, zero third-party exposure."

otel.heading: Built on top of existing telemetry
otel.description: Ember's data starts with the Forge compiler manifest — a JSON file emitted on every build that lists every skill, version, hash, agent target, and token estimate. No hooks needed. Then it grows with integrations.

claudeCode.title: Tier 1 — Forge Manifest
claudeCode.description: Which skills, which versions, which agents, per project. Version drift detection across developers. Token budget utilization per agent.

ember.title: Tier 2 — Langfuse / Helicone
ember.description: Correlate manifest data with actual LLM usage. Answer: 'skill X v2.1 costs 40% more tokens than v2.0.' Aggregate across tools.

combined.title: Tier 3 — Agent OTEL
combined.description: Ingest native agent telemetry (Claude Code OTEL, Cline logs). Confirm which skills were actually activated, not just deployed.

otel.footer: Each tier adds a new data dimension without replacing the previous one. Start with manifest analytics, grow into full observability.

dashboard.heading: What you'll see
dashboard.caption: Mock data — illustrates what Ember dashboards will provide. Push to Grafana, DataDog, or any OTLP-compatible backend.

landscape.heading: How Ember fits the landscape
landscape.footer: Ember doesn't compete with any of these. It's the unified collector that covers all AI assistants and pushes to your choice of backend.
